tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: A batsman hits back a ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> straight in the direction of the bowler without changing its initial speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The impulse imparted to the ball is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Impulse, J=∫Fdt=Change in momentum

Therefore,
Impulse, Δp=mv--mv=2mv=2×0.4×15 =12 N s
